items.summary: The read-only mode can be bypassed on the MySQL and MariaDB connectors. In read-only mode a caller can still execute arbitrary write and DDL statements (for example DROP TABLE), which defeats the protection that read-only mode is meant to provide when a database is exposed to an AI agent. Root cause The problem is a mismatch between how DBHub's SQL parser handles single-line comments and how MySQL and MariaDB actually parse them. items.title: SD JWT JS: Tampered disclosures silently dropped instead of rejected
items.summary: ## Summary When one Disclosure in an SD-JWT presentation is tampered so its digest no longer matches the Issuer-signed `_sd` array, `@sd-jwt/decode` 0.19.0 does **not** reject the presentation. It silently drops the unmatched Disclosure and returns a **reduced claim set**, reporting success. The Issuer signature is untouched and valid. This is a downgrade/omission primitive.
